note: Built around the Tower Hall Theatre Foundation's 16-volume Tower Hall Nurthi Gee series (℗ 2023 Tower Studio; recording dates and singers not given), which revives the old Tower Hall stage songs, with Siri Sangabo-related pieces (Siri Sanga Bodhi, Boho Sen Anuradhapuraye, Kethkule Wu Sangathissa, Oba Hata Yalu Sangabo) and Ramayana-themed ones. Danno Budunge, from John de Silva's Siri Sangabo (1903), appears in the two renditions the FT singles out (Rukmani Devi and Amaradeva); Lona Muni Rajage is a modern rendition of a song Wikipedia calls a nurti song. Which play each Tower Hall track comes from is read from its title only.

size.basis: No source counts nurthi recordings. What was read: the first recorded Sinhala song was a nurthi song (Othello's "Deweni Lokapathi", Sinhala Wikipedia) and English Wikipedia names a 1903 album Nurthi; P. Orr & Co. of Madras recorded some of John de Silva's songs in 1908; Vishwanath Lavji alone had nearly 280 tunes to his credit; radio kept 'A-grade nurti singers' (Ramya Wanigasekara, Shrilal Abeykoon) and a Nurthi Gee programme; Gerald Wickremesooriya produced a Nurthi Gee record; the Tower Hall Theatre Foundation's Tower Hall Nurthi Gee series on iTunes Sri Lanka is 16 volumes of 13-15 tracks (about 235 tracks, some repeated). Old 78s, radio transcriptions and cassettes are mostly not on any readable catalogue. A few hundred distinct songs survive in the repertoire; with re-recordings by later singers (Danno Budunge alone has over 20 versions on iTunes) the total is perhaps 300-1500. An insider's essential list would be about 30 songs, mostly from John de Silva's plays (Siri Sangabo, Ramayanaya, Sri Wickrama). A judgement, not a count.
